payload.unusable_reason: Not a motor accident compensation claim for death or injury: the insured truck owner's consumer complaint against his own insurer for damage to the truck (own-damage claim), decided by consumer fora, not a Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal.

journey.note: Insured truck owner's appeal against the National Commission's 2015 dismissal of his own-damage claim allowed: the district forum's 2014 order for Rs 4,93,500 restored, interest raised to 9% a year, plus a composite Rs 1,00,000 for costs and agony. Not a MACT award; no total stated.

extraction.title_anon: Truck owner's own-damage insurance claim, Chhattisgarh (not a death or injury claim)
extraction.family_summary: In November 2011 a loaded goods truck overturned into a river in Jharkhand; this was a claim for damage to the truck, not for death or injury. The owner's insurer refused to pay, saying he had sold the truck in 2008, but in 2014 the district consumer forum in Chhattisgarh ordered it to pay Rs 4,93,500 with 6% interest, and the state commission agreed. The National Commission dismissed the claim in 2015. In June 2020, about eight and a half years after the accident, the Supreme Court restored the forum's order, raised interest to 9% and added Rs 1,00,000 for costs and agony.
what_mattered: On the accident date the truck was still registered, permitted and insured in the owner's name and he was still repaying the bank loan, so the 2008 sale agreement had not transferred ownership.

The Supreme Court held that under section 2(30) of the Motor Vehicles Act the registered owner remains the owner, so the insurer could not refuse his own claim because of the sale agreement; short delays in the police report and the claim did not defeat it.
